Family intake and consent

2nd Chance Housing, Inc. Researcher training · Draft for organizational and counsel review · Statutes and official pages last read 10/29/2026 · Not legal advice.

DRAFT, not approved. The consent text below is a starting point for 2nd Chance's leadership and counsel to review, correct and approve before any family signs it. Use only the version your supervisor issues. It is not legal advice.

Part 1: Consent (read aloud, then sign)

Who we are. 2nd Chance Housing, Inc. is a nonprofit. We are not a law firm and not part of any court or government office. We cannot give legal advice.

What we offer. With your permission, we help you gather and organize facts and papers about the property and family of , so a lawyer can review them.

What we cannot promise. We cannot promise that a lawyer will take the case, that any help will be free, who owns the property, whether you qualify for anything, or any result. A lawyer, the court or a title company decides.

I give permission for 2nd Chance Housing to (check each that applies):

  • Collect documents and facts about the person who died, the property, and my family.
  • Store them in 2nd Chance's secure system and files for: ______________ (period to be set by the organization).
  • Share them with this lawyer or organization: ______________________________.
  • Share them with a title company, only if I say so later in writing.
  • Contact me by (check): ☐ email ☐ phone ☐ text ☐ in person. Best times: __________ . Do not contact me: __________ .

Who may speak for our family: ______________________________   Who should not be told yet: ______________________________

My rights. I may say no, ask 2nd Chance to stop, or ask 2nd Chance to delete what it holds, at any time, by contacting ______________________ . Declining changes nothing about how I am treated.

Signature (family contact)
Printed name, relationship, date
Researcher (name, date)
Supervisor review (name, date)

Questions for counsel on this form: retention period; whether Illinois privacy law adds requirements; whether a witness or notary is wise; wording for minors and incapacitated persons; sharing with a title company.

Part 2: Intake interview

ItemAnswer and source (who said it, or which record)
Person who died: full legal name; other names
Date and place of death; source
County where she lived at death
Marital status; every spouse or partner, ever
Every child (adopted, earlier relationships, deceased), with dates of any death
Property address; every PIN
Who lives there; rent; tenants; deposits; who collects rent now
Insurance (company, renewal, vacant or occupied)
Taxes owed; mortgage or HELOC; liens known
Will, trust or TODI? Who holds the original?
Existing estate case? Lawyer already acting?
Accounts, vehicles, other assets (last four digits only)
Funeral costs; who paid; other debts
Medicaid received?
Urgent issues (tax sale, foreclosure, insurance, danger, lawsuit)
Their goal (their words)

Collect only what the family agrees to share and the case needs. Anything said is a lead until you see the record.
